diagnostic_evidence.quote: The Runge--Kutta method \cref{eq:RK} is called AS-stable if $I - z A$ is non-singular for all $z \in \C^-$ and $z b^T (I - z A)^{-1}$ is uniformly bounded for $z \in \C^-$.

issues.failure_explanation: To apply Theorem Nevanlinna one must verify the hypothesis ||D(z)|| <= 1 for all z in C^-. With D(z) = alpha z b^T (I-zA)^{-1} and the stated alpha^{-1} = sup ||b^T (I-zA)^{-1}||, the quantity to bound is ||D(z)|| = alpha |z| ||b^T (I-zA)^{-1}||, i.e. it carries an extra factor |z| that the chosen normalization does not control. The hypothesis AS-stability bounds sup ||z b^T (I-zA)^{-1}||, not sup ||b^T (I-zA)^{-1}||, so with the printed alpha the contraction property ||D(z)|| <= 1 is neither established nor true in general (e.g. the scalar method A=(a), b=(1) with 0<a<1 has sup_{C^-}|1/(1-az)| = 1 but sup|z/(1-az)| = 1/a > 1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the normalization by alpha^{-1} = sup_{z in C^-} ||z b^T (I - zA)^{-1}||, which is finite by AS-stability, and note that ||D(z)|| <= 1 then holds; the lemma statement and all dependent results are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform boundedness of (b^T \otimes Z)(I - A\otimes Z)^{-1}, used to bound the stiff parts of the LTE recursion (eq:LTE_coeffs) and of the stability term in the C-stability argument, is left unsupported as written; with the corrected normalization the lemma itself and all downstream results hold unchanged.
issues.title: Wrong normalization constant when applying Nevanlinna's theorem to zb^T(I-zA)^{-1}
issues.why_classification: A one-line redefinition of alpha (using the AS-stability bound sup||zb^T(I-zA)^{-1}|| instead of sup||b^T(I-zA)^{-1}||) completes the proof; the lemma's conclusion and every downstream guarantee survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Rows 5g and 5h of Table tab:order_conditions display two distinct rooted trees of order 5 but print byte-identical order conditions b^T A^{i_1+i_2+1} C A^{i_3}(c^2/2 - A c). Applying Definition def:semilinear_order to the path-type tree shown in row 5h (a chain ending in a two-leaf cherry, with no lone-leaf children at internal vertices) yields V-spaces generated with C^0 factors and bottom residual gamma_3, so its condition is b^T A^{i_1+i_2+i_3+1}(c^3/6 - A c^2/2) = 0, involving no C factor; the formula printed in row 5h (with the C factor and residual gamma_2) is the condition belonging to the tree of row 5g. Hence at least one of the two rows states a condition that is not the semilinear order condition of the tree next to it, and the 'Implied By: 3a' entry of that row is likewise inconsistent with the printed formula (the printed C*gamma_2-type condition follows from row 4b/C(2), not from 3a).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the formula in row 5h by the condition generated by Definition def:semilinear_order for that tree, b^T A^{i_1+i_2+i_3+1}(c^3/6 - A c^2/2) = 0 for all i_1,i_2,i_3 (equivalently, correct the 'Implied By' entry of the other row to 4b), and verify the remaining rows the same way.
issues.overall_effect: One row of the central table of semilinear order conditions (tab:order_conditions) asserts a condition that is not the one Definition def:semilinear_order assigns to the displayed tree; a reader imposing conditions from the table imposes a wrong constraint for that tree. The row is redundant (the correct condition is implied by 3a), so no downstream theorem or constructed method is invalidated.
issues.title: Order condition printed for tree 5h duplicates row 5g and does not match its tree
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local correction of one displayed formula using the paper's own Definition def:semilinear_order; the affected condition is redundant (implied by 3a), so every formal result, guarantee, and constructed method is unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The top row displays reference methods that satisfy the classical order conditions up to the respective orders ($p = 4$ for left and middle, and $p = 5$ on the right), but not any of the (other) semilinear order conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose asserts that the slope-2 envelope of the error curves of the top-row reference methods 'matches the B-convergence order indicated by the theory, i.e., the error estimate \cref{thm:convergence}'. For those reference methods, which have semilinear order p_SL = 1 and classical order p = 4 or 5, the cited Theorem thm:convergence gives q = p_SL = 1 (the superconvergent case q = p_SL + 1 = 2 requires p = p_SL + 1), i.e. an O(h) bound corresponding to a line of slope 1, not 2. The observed slope-2 envelope is therefore not what the paper's own theory indicates for these methods; the prose claims agreement with a guarantee the theory does not provide.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, (iii)~the family of error curves, parameterized by $\lambda$, lies uniformly below a line of slope 2, matching the B-convergence order indicated by the theory, i.e., the error estimate \cref{thm:convergence}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the sentence to state the envelope the theory actually provides for the reference methods (order q = p_SL = 1, or 'at least' the observed slope), without attributing the slope-2 envelope to Theorem thm:convergence.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical section misstates what the paper's convergence theorem predicts for the reference methods (order 2 instead of the guaranteed order q = p_SL = 1); the formal results themselves are unaffected.
issues.title: Prose attributes a slope-2 error envelope to the theory for stage-order-1 reference methods
issues.why_classification: A local rewording of one sentence restores agreement with the formal results; no theorem, guarantee, or rate in the paper is affected.
